children.text: Burias Island is the island of Masbate province closest to mainland Luzon. Its trips center on island hopping from San Pascual to small islands such as Sombrero Island, the Tinalisayan sandbar and the Animasola cliffs. Electricity, signal and cash are scarce, so preparation is needed.

Burias Island is one of the three big islands of Masbate province in the Bicol region, which together with Masbate Island and Ticao Island make up the province. It faces Ragay Gulf to the north and the Ticao and Burias passes to the south and east, and the island is divided between two municipalities, San Pascual in the north and Claveria in the south. San Pascual, the center for travel, has an area of about 246.65 sq km and a 2024 population of about 44,641. Claveria covers about 182.98 sq km with a population of about 40,733 and is said to lie about 352 km southeast of Manila. The name Claveria is said to come from the Spanish governor-general Narciso Claveria y Zaldua, who anchored nearby in 1844 while chasing Moro pirates. It became a town in 1898, fell back to a barrio after a cholera epidemic in 1901, and was re-established as a municipality in 1959. San Pascual includes the northern part of the island, Busing and Templo (Iniwaran) islands and six small uninhabited islets.

The heart of a trip is island hopping. The small islands under San Pascual, Sombrero, Tinalisayan, Animasola and Dapa, are the standard circuit. Sombrero Island is known for a rock resembling a cowboy hat, a white-sand beach and sunsets over the Sibuyan Sea, and it is the base for overnight stays. Tinalisayan is a white sandbar exposed mostly at low tide, while Animasola has sandstone cliffs and tide pools reachable at low tide, and sturdy aqua shoes are described as essential. Dapa Island (Snake Island) is known for cliff jumping, but it is said to be home to venomous yellow-lipped sea kraits, so be careful. Ambulong Island, Virgin Island (which has a resort), Tinalisayan Daku and Tanguingui Island are also mentioned on hopping routes, and some visitors take a side trip to Alibijaban Island in San Andres, Quezon. Activities are simple: snorkeling, freediving, scuba, kayaking, watching sunrise and sunset, and camping. It is safer to bring your own gear.

The island's charm is simplicity rather than polish. In town there are an old church, Spanish-style ancestral houses and the old municipal hall, and one guide calls San Pascual Church the oldest church in Bicol. The Balinsasayaw House is said to hold more than 80,000 swiftlets, and around May 12–17 the rodeo-style Isla Rancho Festival is held. A guide mentions San Isidro Beach, with white sand, on the Claveria side. One source says the overland trip between the two municipalities is about 124 km and takes 3 hours 45 minutes to 4 hours, so trying to see both in one day is unrealistic.

This is a destination that requires preparation. There are no ATMs on the island and cards are not accepted, and a recent blog said only 9 of San Pascual's 22 barangays have electricity and that power in town generally runs from about 5 PM to 5 AM. The generator on Sombrero Island is said to run only from 6 PM to 6 AM. Mobile signal is often available only near the municipal hall and the plaza. Because of sea and weather restrictions, the Coast Guard frequently issues no-sail orders from June to October, so go in the dry season if possible. Fares and boat times differ between sources and must be confirmed locally. The climate is warm year-round, with mean daily highs of about
and annual rainfall of about 1,578 mm.

With cliffs and a small cove, it is known for cliff jumping. It is said to be home to venomous yellow-lipped sea kraits, so do not put your hand into rock crevices or touch any snake. Entry is reported to be free.
An old church, Spanish-style ancestral houses and the old municipal hall remain, and the Balinsasayaw House is said to be home to more than 80,000 swiftlets. Stop by before or after hopping.
Rodeo-style events are reported to be held in San Pascual around May 12–17. The schedule differs from year to year, so check the latest announcement.
Staying a night on Sombrero or Tinalisayan gives you sunsets and stars. With electricity limited, the nights are dark and quiet.

items.title: 2 days 1 night hopping
items.subtitle: Cross from Pasacao and stay a night on Sombrero

children.text: Take a jeepney from Naga to Pasacao Port. It is said to take about 30 minutes.
Board the boat from Pasacao to San Pascual. It takes 2–3 hours.
At San Pascual port, register at the tourism office, find a boat and go to Sombrero and Tinalisayan.
Watch the sunset on Sombrero Island and have dinner.
On day two, after sunrise, visit Animasola and Dapa islands.
Return to town, see the church and ancestral houses, and check the last boat time.
One source says boats are better leaving between 5:30 and 8:00 AM. The sea can be rougher in the afternoon.

items.title: 3 days 2 nights
items.subtitle: Island hopping and an unhurried town

children.text: On the first day, arrive in San Pascual, find lodging and look around town.
On day two, tour Sombrero, Tinalisayan, Animasola and Dapa, and stay a night on Sombrero.
On day three, watch the sunrise, return to San Pascual and take the boat home.
If you miss the last boat, you must stay another night on the island.

items.title: From Manila to Masbate and Claveria

children.text: An old guide says the boat from Masbate City to San Pascual runs only on Tuesdays and Saturdays, taking 8–9 hours.
Claveria is about 3 hours by RORO from Pio Duran in Albay. From Claveria to San Pascual it is about
124km
overland.
In San Pascual, tricycles and habal-habal (motorcycles) are the main transport.
Register your hopping boat at the tourism office at the port. Guides say it starts at about
per day for six people, while others say

A recent source names March to late May as the best time and November–December as an alternative with remaining typhoon risk. From June to October the Coast Guard often issues no-sail orders. The afternoon sea is reported to be rougher than the morning, so take boats early in the morning.
In mid-May the Isla Rancho Festival may be held, and lodging fills up early. Schedules can change from year to year.

Burias is an outlying island away from the mainland, so a single stretch of weather can push your whole itinerary back. If you have an international flight or connection, leave at least one spare day on the return. The first jeepney from Naga to Pasacao is said to leave around 5:30 AM, so if you want the morning boat it is easier to stay in Naga the night before. Boats back from San Pascual are listed at times such as 5:30 AM, 9:30 AM and 2:30 PM (public outriggers), but these can change from year to year.

In town, simple lodgings are reported: Sunset View Tourist Inn (about
), MSS Fuentes Lodging (about
) and Virjen Island Resort (from about
). There are no high-end hotels. Sombrero Island has cottages and tents, with prices that vary widely by season and facilities.

There are no restaurants on the outer islands, only small shops on Sombrero. The usual method is to buy ingredients at the Pasacao or San Andres markets and ask the boat crew or a caretaker to cook. A drum of water is said to be about
. Withdraw cash in advance in Naga, Pasacao or San Andres.

Have dinner at a restaurant in town or at your lodging, and for lunch on hopping days it is best to ask the boatman or prepare a packed lunch. Many visitors are said to eat dinner at a restaurant serving Bicol food in Naga before setting out. Fresh water is scarce on the islands, so use showers and dishwashing sparingly.
Bring plenty of cash. There are no ATMs on the island and cards are not accepted.
Bring a power bank and a flashlight. Electricity is limited.
Put your camera and phone in a waterproof bag for the boat.
Taking boats early in the morning means calmer waves.
Take all your trash with you. There is no disposal on the islands.
Register and find a boat at the tourism office at San Pascual port.
Buy your return ticket from Naga to Manila as soon as you arrive.
Evening boats stop early. Check the last boat time.
When the Coast Guard issues a no-sail order, boats do not run. This is especially frequent from June to October, so leave a day or two of slack.
Medical care is about the San Pascual rural health unit. Serious cases must go to Naga or the Eastern Bicol Medical Center.
The yellow-lipped sea kraits of Dapa Island are venomous. Do not touch them.
Animasola and Tinalisayan have no shade, so watch for heatstroke.
The trip is not recommended for pregnant travelers, infants or people with limited mobility, according to one guide.
Fares and schedules differ widely between sources, so be sure to confirm locally.
